facts.fact: TTCL, through the National ICT Broadband Backbone, and Burundi Backbone System agreed to raise connectivity capacity to Burundi from 4Gbps to 10Gbps, so a terrestrial Tanzania-Burundi link was already carrying 4Gbps; reported by Tech Africa News on 9 September 2026.

ARCT's 2020 ICT indicators report (July 2021) states Burundi has access to submarine cables (EASSy, SEACOM, TEAMS) via partners and cable operators in neighbouring countries, and lists cross-border fibre connection points with Rwanda (Gasenyi, Kanyaru Haut), the DRC (Ruhwa, Gatumba) and Tanzania (Kobero, Mugina/Manyovu); no per-route traffic or in-service dates are given, and no date is stated beyond the report's own (published 2021-07).

facts.fact: Burundi Backbone System connects to Tanzania's NICTBB at Kabanga and Manyovu under a contract begun in 2019 and renewed for five years in February 2024.

Internet Society's report lists no submarine cable for Burundi, terrestrial cross-border links to the Democratic Republic of Congo, Rwanda and Tanzania, and says Burundi relies mainly on SEACOM and EASSy for cloud access in South Africa.

Agence Ecofin reports that landlocked Burundi relies on Tanzania's cables, and that Tanzania's TTCL signed a five-year USD 3.3 million deal to resell high-speed capacity to Burundi Backbone System, after an October 2019 accord.

note: Only a gateway-competition level; states no route or capacity sale.
